rationale: Semantic review of the second artifact for C1-recovery-adopts-committed-vector. The first property (adoption at the resolution) corresponds to the written obligation; the added accept-round property does not, because its observation never reaches the accept reply it is meant to judge. I traced the harness schedule against the retained stream and the handlers, and the item is recorded as revision_needed with the observation as the challenged component so the consequence is not treated as confirmed.

review_items.report_title: 接受轮次观察未命中前提
review_items.report_answer: 第二个属性的观测并未覆盖它要判断的接受回复：harness 的分辨率事件之后实际投递的是阶段一重启的 PreAccept 及其 PreAcceptReply，acceptOKs 读数为 0→0（reply_counted=false），accept_round_after_commit 事件在已提交副本的 AcceptReply 尚未产生、也未回投之前就被打印。因此该违反结论是观测/驱动缺陷，不能作为接受轮次后果的证据；采用采纳属性的第一条属性不受影响。
review_items.rationale: Requirement versus predicate: the added property asserts reply_counted on the accept_round_after_commit event, which is meant to encode that the accept round keeps a continuation when the only available replica has already committed the instance. Entry and schedule: after the resolution, handlePrepareReply runs sub-case 6 and calls startPhase1, which replaces InstanceSpace[1][0] with a new PREACCEPTED record and queues a PreAccept (code 11), not an Accept. The harness then drains that PreAccept into the committed replica, whose handlePreAccept branch replies with Status COMMITTED (its >= ACCEPTED branch writes the incoming command into InstanceSpace[preAccept.LeaderId][0]), and delivering that PreAcceptReply is what makes the recoverer enter ACCEPTED and queue an Accept (code 13, visible only in the later diagnostic event's out_codes). So when the event is emitted, the accept reply has neither been produced nor delivered: the accept_oks_before/after 0 to 0 reading reflects the phase-1 reply, not the accept round, and instance_status_after ACCEPTED records the transition caused by the PreAcceptReply rather than a completed accept attempt. Oracle: because the observed sequence is the wrong round, the predicate cannot establish or refute the continuation question; the violation is an artefact of the schedule and of reading acceptOKs at the wrong point. The repair is to drive the round explicitly after the resolution: drain the queued messages, assert which message code was produced as a control, deliver the Accept to the committed replica and its AcceptReply back, and only then read acceptOKs, the leader bookkeeping status and the record status from the record currently in InstanceSpace. The first property, its prerequisite and its violated witness are unaffected and stay as reviewed.
limitations: the review of the first property (adoption at the resolution) is unchanged and remains valid for the earlier artifact and this one
the consequence question (whether the recovery can complete, and whether the row then stalls) remains open until a corrected accept-round observation is executed
counterevidence: scoped to the executed stream (check d5769994f11746fba640e2057fbd13b8): the accept_round_after_commit event reports accept_oks_before 0 and accept_oks_after 0 while instance_status_after is ACCEPTED, and the first accept code appears only in the trailing diagnostic event's out_codes, which shows the Accept was queued after the PreAcceptReply was delivered rather than by the resolution itself (S15-handlePrepareReply, S11-handleAccept)

scoped to the handlers: handlePreAccept on a record whose status is already COMMITTED replies with Status COMMITTED from its status >= ACCEPTED branch, and that reply is what moves the recoverer to ACCEPTED and queues the Accept; the committed replica's AcceptReply is therefore not what the harness observed (S9-handlePreAccept, S11-handleAccept, S12-handleAcceptReply)
